verdict.rationale: Babylon.js is fundamentally API/code-first (NPM modules, TypeScript, ES6 tree-shaking) and its visual tools — Inspector, Node Material Editor, Playground — are built on top of that same scene graph and material system, implying most visual editing corresponds to API objects. However, the evidence never explicitly states that actions performed in the Inspector or NME can be reproduced or exported 1:1 through code, nor does it document any API-vs-UI parity guarantee. missing for 10: explicit documentation or example showing Inspector/NME edits exported as equivalent API code, independent confirmation of full UI-API parity, and any mention of gaps where UI tools expose functionality not otherwise scriptable.
